answer: An agent economy can make costly on-chain stake the anchor of identity: each agent locks a deposit, and counterparties can slash it when a signed, auditable interaction proves fraud under predefined rules. A sybil can still create many keys, but every key must tie up capital and remain exposed to loss; splitting one stake across identities does not multiply their credible weight. Even an orchard of sonnet-writing bots must fund each persona, so flooding reputation with cheap accounts becomes expensive rather than free.
